title: Sharkey's record dates and Fazola's first Bob Crosby session
summary: He spoke on Mud Hole Blues and went with a nervous Fazola to his first Crosby date, where his humming of the Bobcats chorus was recorded.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Now up in New York, who was Sharky using for you one day?

Nobody. I'm the first one he used. Because he got the job at Nix you see. He had some record dates and Fazola played with him on the record dates, the first dates. Because I went to the rehearsal, I mean to the recording sessions with him. And I even spoke on one record and didn't play. What did you say? Somebody said, Benny Pollack got the date for Sharky and he played drums. And the opening lines was, hey Sharky, what you doing up here in New York? And I answered, I said, man can't you see I'm trying to play the blues? Or a thing called Mud Hole Blues. Did you ever hear that record? I think I have it.

And I went with Fazola the first session he made with Bob Crosby. I went with him and he was nervous. He was shaking like a leaf. He said, come with me Bill. He says, man I'm scared. I said you're scared to play with those fellas. I said you should know those fellas better than anybody else. I mean, from your own hometown. He had played with Claude Thornhill and everybody else and he was scared to play with Bob Crossford's band. So they were stuck for something to play and I suggested that the March of the Bobcats, which wasn't called that. We used to sing it as John McDonough in the grammar schools. And Papa Celestan originated the trumpet chorus. You remember the chorus they used to that? Oh yeah, I know the trumpet chorus. I hummed it to Yank Lawson at the recording session and they cut it right there. And it more or less was my brainchild that they made so much money on. And it was a real spontaneous chorus Fazola took. He didn't practice anything else. He just played it and that was it.
And that was his first session with the Bob Crossford band.
Then he went to work with them steady, you see. His first job with them was the record date.
